stops.note: a place-surname, 'the side of the burn', burn being the Scots and northern word for a stream
after Ambrose Burnside, the Union general defeated at Fredericksburg in 1862, famous for bushy whiskers joined to his moustache above a shaved chin
the two halves were swapped, perhaps because the whiskers grow on the side of the face
stops.meaning: hair on the side of the face

current_meaning: strips of hair grown down the sides of a man's face
